reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: annealing CrCoNi to induce short-range order (SRO) is known to increase strength and can plausibly improve fracture resistance via crack-tip shielding, though simultaneously enhancing ductility and modulus is less certain and depends on an unproven optimal SRO level.
reasons.testability: The test is clear and feasible, using APT to quantify SRO and standard mechanical tests, but the falsification criterion is too broad—it requires improvement in all four properties, so a null result in one (e.g., modulus) would falsify the hypothesis even if the mechanism is partially correct.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful for researchers, as it proposes a simple, controllable processing route to optimize multiple properties in a well-studied alloy system, directly addressing the research question.
